coaching.coaching: Add a regression test covering the None-on-OSError contract of build_alias_index.
coaching.subject: the None-on-OSError contract of build_alias_index

evidence: src/rebar/_ids.py:334-349: `alias_matches = (alias_index.get(ticket_id, []) if alias_index is not None else _scan_alias(...))` then `if len(alias_matches) > 1: ... return None`
Docstring claim src/rebar/_ids.py:284-285: 'The result is identical to per-call scanning (same match set, same ambiguity handling).'

tests/unit/test_referencing_commits_alias_scan_perf.py builds only distinct single-match aliases (`decoy_aliases = [_new_ticket_alias(...) for i in range(6)]`), so the indexed >1-match ambiguity branch is never driven.
src/rebar/_ids.py:334-338: `if alias_index is not None else _scan_alias(ticket_id, tracker_dir)`
src/rebar/_ids.py:229-233: build_alias_index returns None on OSError listing the tracker
src/rebar/_engine_support/commit_impact.py:194-199 comment: '`None` (tracker unreadable) falls back to per-call scanning, preserving behavior.'
tests/unit/test_referencing_commits_alias_scan_perf.py uses a normal readable tracker, so build_alias_index never returns None and the fallback branch is not exercised.
dropped.finding: The newly-added indexed alias-resolution path (alias_index.get returning a multi-element list) has no test, though the resolver docstring contracts 'same ambiguity handling' as per-call scanning. When two ticket directories share one effective alias, build_alias_index groups both names under that alias and resolve_ticket_id must hit the len(alias_matches) > 1 branch and return None; the new test only exercises distinct single-match aliases.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that build_alias_index returns None for an unreadable/nonexistent tracker_dir.
evidence: src/rebar/_ids.py:225 docstring: 'Returns None on a hard failure listing the tracker (so the caller can fall back to per-call scanning)'
src/rebar/_ids.py:229-233 the try/except OSError -> return None branch is newly added

ABSENCE: search_files for build_alias_index in tests/ finds only the happy-path call at test_referencing_commits_alias_scan_perf.py:121; no test invokes it against an unreadable/nonexistent tracker_dir to assert None
dropped.finding: The documented contract that build_alias_index returns None on a hard tracker-listing failure (the fallback signal callers rely on) has no test.
scenarios: A caller passes a tracker_dir that cannot be listed (missing/permission-denied); the None fallback contract silently regresses to returning {} or raising, and no test catches it

src/rebar/_engine_support/commit_impact.py:197 comment: '`None` (tracker unreadable) falls back to per-call scanning, preserving behavior.'

ABSENCE: test_indexed_resolution_matches_per_call_scanning always passes alias_index=index for the indexed path and never passes alias_index=None explicitly to confirm the fallback resolves via _scan_alias identically
dropped.finding: The alias_index=None fallback branch of resolve_ticket_id (documented to 'fall back to per-call scanning, preserving behavior') is never exercised by the new tests.
scenarios: build_alias_index returns None on a large store during a real close; the None value flows into resolve_ticket_id and must still resolve every commit trailer via _scan_alias — an untested path
